additions.reason: Central concept of Torah #106. The Rebbe builds the entire teaching around the move from katnut to gadlut hamochin. When gadlut is reached, the Talmudic dictum 'great is da'at that was placed between two letters (El and YHVH)' applies: chesed and rachamim are awakened. Gadlut hamochin is the dominant node of Package 1 — it is explicitly the state that activates da'at and draws chesed (El) and rachamim (YHVH).

additions.reason: Da'at is the central positive concept. The Rebbe opens by citing 'there is no poverty but poverty of da'at' and builds toward the Talmudic statement 'great is da'at given between two letters (El and YHVH)'. Da'at is the state-bridge: its absence = katnut/aniyut (Package 2); its presence = gadlut (Package 1). Da'at is a bechina of gadlut hamochin — they are two faces of the same state of expanded consciousness.

additions.reason: Katnut hamochin is the dominant node of Package 2. The Rebbe explicitly names this state using the bechina marker 'nikra': 'there are times when one has no sekhel, and it is called katnut hamochin'. This is the exact evil mirror of gadlut hamochin — the same dimension of consciousness, but diminished. Under katnut, da'at is absent, dinim are not sweetened, and the person cannot ascend to chesed and rachamim without help.

additions.reason: Aniyut (spiritual poverty) is the Rebbe's opening concept. The Talmudic dictum 'ein aniyut ela min hada'at' (Nedarim 41) establishes poverty as a bechina of lacking da'at — the two are the same condition from different angles. The Rebbe specifies this poverty exists both collectively (a person who lacks sekhel in divine service needs the wise to guide him) and individually (a person who himself falls into katnut). It is a bechina of katnut hamochin, not a cause or consequence.
additions.source_quote: אִיתָא, דְּאֵין עֲנִיּוּת אֶלָּא מִן הַדַּעַת

proposed_bechina_edges.proof_text: Katnut = no sekhel = no da'at = aniyut — all expressions of the same deficiency state

additions.reason: The word 'dal' in the verse 'ashrei maskil el dal' is explicitly interpreted by the Rebbe as referring to the person who is in katnut hamochin: 'namely, when he is in katnut hamochin'. Dal is thus a bechina of katnut — the verse's 'poor person' IS the one in diminished consciousness. This also connects to עניות (aniyut = spiritual poverty = dal) and to the Torah #1 concept of 'dal' (poor/receiving), but here in Torah #106 the dal refers specifically and only to the one in katnut.

additions.reason: Absence/deficiency of da'at is the root definition of both aniyut and katnut hamochin. The Talmudic source 'ein aniyut ela min hada'at' makes lack of da'at the universal root of spiritual poverty. This is the conceptual opposite of 'daat' in Package 1 — same axis, opposite pole. The absence of da'at = katnut = dal = aniyut, while presence of da'at = gadlut = chesed + rachamim.
